name: Social Media News Feed
description: Design a social media news feed like Facebook or Instagram. Covers feed generation (fanout on write vs read), ML-based ranking, caching, and real-time updates.

learnSteps.title: Fanout on Write (Push Model)
learnSteps.description: When a user publishes a post, the Fanout Worker pushes the post ID into every follower's feed list in Redis. For a user with 1,000 followers, this means 1,000 Redis writes. This pre-computes feeds so reads are instant (O(1) cache lookup). The trade-off: write amplification is high for users with millions of followers (celebrities).

learnSteps.title: Hybrid Fanout Strategy
learnSteps.description: For celebrity users (1M+ followers), fanout on write is too expensive. Instead, the system uses fanout on read for celebrities: when a user loads their feed, the Feed Service merges their pre-computed feed (from Redis) with recent posts from celebrities they follow (queried from MongoDB at read time). This hybrid approach caps write amplification.

learnSteps.title: ML-Based Feed Ranking
learnSteps.description: The raw feed (chronological post IDs) is passed to the Feed Ranking Model. It scores each post using signals: user affinity, post engagement (likes, comments), content type, recency, and creator quality. The model reorders the feed to maximize engagement. A/B testing different ranking models is done via feature flags.

learnSteps.title: Feed Cache and Pagination
learnSteps.description: Each user's feed is a Redis sorted set (score = timestamp or ranking score). The Feed Service reads the top N items with ZREVRANGE for the first page and cursor-based pagination for subsequent pages. The cache holds the latest ~500 posts per user. Stale feeds (inactive users) are evicted via volatile-lru. On cache miss, the feed is regenerated from the social graph DB.

chaosScenarios.name: Feed Cache Shard Loss
chaosScenarios.description: Crash a Redis shard holding pre-computed feeds for a slice of the user base
chaosScenarios.expectedBehavior: Users mapped to the lost shard get cold feeds. Regeneration fans out to the social graph DB and post store, multiplying read load 10-20x for those users; p99 feed load jumps from ~300ms to multi-second until rewarm completes.
mitigationSteps: Serve a degraded chronological feed from MongoDB while regeneration runs
Coalesce regeneration so each user feed is rebuilt exactly once (singleflight)
Rate-limit rebuilds to protect the PostgreSQL graph DB
Rewarm most-active users first using last-seen data

chaosScenarios.name: Ranking Model Brownout
chaosScenarios.description: Inject latency into the feed ranking model until inference exceeds its 50ms budget
chaosScenarios.expectedBehavior: Inference p99 rises past the timeout. The Feed Service trips the ranking circuit breaker and serves chronological ordering; feeds stay available with degraded relevance. Engagement metrics dip but the error rate stays flat.
mitigationSteps: Confirm the circuit breaker opened and chronological fallback is engaged
Shed ranking for long-tail users first; keep it for high-engagement cohorts
Scale inference replicas or roll back the latest model deploy
Close the breaker gradually with canary traffic

chaosScenarios.name: Fanout Worker Backlog
chaosScenarios.description: Choke the fanout worker pool during a viral posting spike, building Kafka consumer lag
chaosScenarios.expectedBehavior: Post publishes succeed but delivery into follower feeds lags; consumer lag grows past tens of millions of events. Reads are unaffected — users instead complain about missing fresh posts.
mitigationSteps: Scale fanout workers on consumer lag
Temporarily demote mega-fanout posts (100k+ followers) to read-time merge
Prioritize partitions carrying high-affinity edges if partitioning supports it
Backfill missed deliveries after the lag drains

bottleneckProgression.description: Cache-miss feed regenerations and follow-graph queries saturate the connection pool across the 5 replicas
bottleneckProgression.resolution: Add read replicas behind a pooler and cache follower lists separately from feeds

bottleneckProgression.description: Ranking inference becomes the per-request critical path; batching queues build and timeouts trip the fallback
bottleneckProgression.resolution: Increase batch size, prune candidate sets before scoring, and add inference replicas or a distilled model

bottleneckProgression.description: The 256GB feed cache starts evicting active feeds; hit rate slides below 0.8, feeding back into graph DB load
bottleneckProgression.resolution: Scale the Redis cluster out, cap feed length per user, and store post IDs + scores only

expectedIssues.title: Celebrity Write Amplification
expectedIssues.description: A single post from a 10M-follower account generates 10M cache writes if pushed, spiking Kafka and Redis simultaneously
expectedIssues.mitigation: Hybrid fanout: posts from accounts above a follower threshold are merged at read time instead of pushed

expectedIssues.title: Feed Regeneration Stampede
expectedIssues.description: Mass eviction or a cold deploy makes thousands of users miss simultaneously, each triggering a full feed rebuild against the graph DB
expectedIssues.mitigation: Singleflight locks per user feed, stale-while-revalidate serving, and jittered TTLs

expectedIssues.title: Pagination Drift and Duplicates
expectedIssues.description: Feeds mutate between page fetches (new posts fanned in, evictions), causing duplicates or gaps with naive offset pagination
expectedIssues.mitigation: Cursor-based pagination anchored to ranking score + post ID instead of offsets

expectedIssues.title: Viral Post Hot Shard
expectedIssues.description: Read-time merges and content hydration for a viral post concentrate on the one MongoDB shard that owns it
expectedIssues.mitigation: Post-content cache in front of MongoDB and replication of hot documents across shards

expectedIssues.title: Duplicate Fanout Deliveries
expectedIssues.description: At-least-once Kafka consumption means retried fanout batches re-insert post IDs into follower feeds
expectedIssues.mitigation: Idempotent feed inserts keyed by post ID (ZADD overwrites rather than duplicates)

slaDefinitions.name: Feed Load Latency
slaDefinitions.penalty: Internal SLO — feed infra review after 2h sustained breach

metrics.name: feed_cache_hit_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of feed loads served from Redis

metrics.name: posts_fanned_out_total
metrics.description: Feed insertions performed by fanout workers

steps: Confirm shard topology and failover state in the Redis cluster
Enable chronological degraded mode for users on the affected shard
Throttle feed regeneration to protect the graph DB
Rewarm feeds ordered by user activity
Check consumer lag per partition to find skew
Scale fanout workers; verify offsets advance
Switch mega-follower accounts to read-time merge
Verify delivery backfill after the lag drains
Compare engagement metrics against the holdout cohort
Roll back to the previous model version
Replay canary traffic against the rolled-back model
Re-enable the new model gradually behind a flag

decisions.title: Hybrid Fanout (Push + Pull)
decisions.context: Pure push amplifies celebrity posts into millions of writes; pure pull makes every feed load query the social graph
decisions.decision: Push post IDs into follower feeds for normal accounts; merge posts from high-follower accounts at read time
consequences: Write amplification is capped regardless of follower count
Feed reads stay O(1) cache lookups for the common case
The read path has two code paths to maintain and test

decisions.title: Ranking Behind a Strict Timeout
decisions.context: ML ranking improves engagement but adds an inference dependency to every feed load
decisions.decision: Call the ranker with a hard latency budget; on timeout or error, serve chronological order
consequences: Feed availability does not depend on model availability
Quality degrades silently, so fallback rate must be monitored as a first-class metric
Model deploys cannot add latency without tripping fallbacks

decisions.title: Separate Graph Store and Post Store
decisions.context: Follow-graph queries are relational; post hydration is high-QPS document reads
decisions.decision: PostgreSQL holds the social graph; sharded MongoDB holds post content
consequences: Each store scales and indexes for its own access pattern
Feed assembly requires cross-store joins in the service layer
Two storage systems to operate and keep consistent

tradeoffs.benefit: p50 feed loads around 80ms from a single cache read
tradeoffs.cost: Millions of speculative cache writes for posts many followers never see

tradeoffs.choice: Eventual delivery with seconds of tolerated fanout lag
tradeoffs.benefit: Publish spikes queue in Kafka instead of failing posts
tradeoffs.cost: Followers may not see a post for 30s+ under load

tradeoffs.benefit: Engagement lift when the model is healthy
tradeoffs.cost: Extra ~10ms on every feed load plus a model-serving fleet to operate

alternatives.name: Pure Fanout-on-Read
alternatives.description: Assemble every feed at request time from followees recent posts
alternatives.prosVsCons: No write amplification or fanout pipeline, but every feed load hits the graph DB and post store, and latency scales with followee count
alternatives.whyNotChosen: At 500k RPS of reads, per-request graph assembly would need an order of magnitude more database capacity

alternatives.name: Pure Fanout-on-Write
alternatives.description: Push every post to every follower, including celebrity accounts
alternatives.prosVsCons: A single simple read path, but a 10M-follower post creates 10M writes and minutes of delivery lag
alternatives.whyNotChosen: Celebrity posts are frequent enough to make worst-case write amplification a steady-state problem

alternatives.name: Pre-Ranked Materialized Feeds
alternatives.description: Run ranking at fanout time and store fully ranked feeds
alternatives.prosVsCons: Removes inference from the read path, but scores go stale immediately and recomputing on every signal change multiplies fanout cost
alternatives.whyNotChosen: Ranking signals like engagement velocity change too fast for write-time scoring to stay accurate
